key_insight: Deep-learning reconstruction enabled whole-body diffusion MRI to run faster while preserving image quality and lesion ADC measurements in metastatic prostate cancer.
clinical_relevance: This approach could shorten whole-body MRI exams for prostate cancer staging and response assessment without sacrificing the quantitative readouts used to characterize bone metastases.
method: Prospective single-centre study at 1.5T with two patient cohorts.
Compared standard WB-DWI with an accelerated DL-reconstructed WB-DWI protocol.
Evaluated image quality with blinded radiologist Likert scoring and lesion ADC agreement with Bland-Altman analysis.
evidence_signal: In 10 patients, image quality remained good-to-excellent across stations, and in 20 patients, lesion ADC values showed no significant difference between standard and accelerated protocols, with a 37% reduction in acquisition time.
watch_item: Small cohorts and single-centre testing mean the findings need broader validation before routine implementation.
paper_title: Evaluation of accelerated whole-body diffusion weighted imaging with deep learning reconstruction in patients with metastatic prostate cancer: assessment of image quality and ADC estimates.
